newsitem.title: UK: ZENECA TURNS LOWER ON LAUNCH COSTS WORRIES.
newsitem.headline: ZENECA TURNS LOWER ON LAUNCH COSTS WORRIES.

text.p: Shares in Zeneca Group Plc, shrugging off strong first-half profits, fell after the company said it faced "substantial" costs in the second half of the year to launch new products.
By 0757 GMT, bucking a firmer market, Zeneca shares were off 39p or 1.91 percent at 20.07-1/2 stg, after opening slightly firmer at 20.54-3/4.

Zeneca Chief Executive Sir David Barnes, in a telephone interview with Reuters, said profit margins were likely to be between two and 2.5 percentage points lower for the full year, taking into account most of the launch costs.
Profit margins rose strongly to 24 percent of sales in the first half of the year from 21.2 percent a year earlier.
The pharmaceuticals and chemicals company earlier said first-half profits jumped by 10 percent to 669 million pounds, well above analysts' forecasts.
Analysts median expectations had been for pre-tax profit of around 649 million pounds.
"Margins were slightly better in the first half and I think the net effect is as expected, but it is the tone of the statement," which is hurting the shares, one analyst said.
BZW analyst Steve Plag said "these were clearly a set of figures which were better than the market anticipated, but with the caveat of substantial launch costs to come in the second half."

But Plag said some analysts seemed to have focused on the performance of some newly-launched drugs, which he said were difficult to predict because of currency impacts and "spotty" approval status around the world.
He said that excluding currency, sales of pharmaceuticals were up 13 percent in the first half of the year, putting Zeneca well up with the best of its British and U.S. peers.
"Overall we are pretty pleased with the results," said Plag, who had been expecting pre-tax profit of 645 million stg.
